title: Redis
subtitle: An in-memory data store for caching, queues and fast shared state.

tiles.label: Strings & hashes
tiles.says: Redis serves keys, strings and hashes from memory.
tiles.detail: Sub-millisecond access removes database load for hot data and sessions.

tiles.label: Lists & sets
tiles.says: Rich structures implement queues, leaderboards and rate limits.
tiles.detail: Atomic commands on structures replace custom code.

tiles.label: TTL & eviction
tiles.says: Keys expire on schedule; eviction frees memory.
tiles.detail: Policies like allkeys-lru make Redis behave as a bounded cache.

tiles.label: Hash slots
tiles.says: Cluster maps keys into 16384 hash slots.
tiles.detail: Each master owns a slot range, so data and load spread across nodes.

tiles.label: MOVED redirects
tiles.says: Clients follow redirects and refresh their slot map.
tiles.detail: Cluster-aware clients route directly, avoiding proxies on the hot path.

tiles.label: Pipelining
tiles.says: Pipelines batch commands into one round trip.

tiles.label: Replication
tiles.detail: Replicas serve reads and stand ready for promotion.

tiles.label: Failover
tiles.says: Cluster promotes a replica when a master is lost.
tiles.detail: Majority agreement over the cluster bus triggers promotion, keeping outages short.

tiles.label: RDB & AOF
tiles.says: Snapshots and append-only logs persist memory to disk.
tiles.detail: Choose recovery point and speed per workload.
